speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand the nature of your symptoms, can you tell me if your double vision worsens when you look sideways or upwards? Additionally, have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the fluctuation with activity is very telling. Given your symptoms of diplopia on vertical gaze and proximal weakness that improves with rest, I need to confirm if you experience any difficulty breathing or speaking during these episodes. Also, do you notice that your eyelids droop more in the evening?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of vertical diplopia, proximal limb weakness that worsens with exertion, and the absence of sensory deficits or family history strongly points to this diagnosis. I recommend requesting antibodies for acetylcholine receptors and MuSK, along with a Tensilon test to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Antibody_Acetylcholine_Receiver; REQUEST TEST: Antibody_MuSK; REQUEST TEST: Tensilon_Test.
